tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

# Refactoring Todo: Maintainability Hotspots

Source: graphify knowledge graph (`graphify-out/graph.json`, 2,206 nodes) plus line counts. Files are ranked by size and cross-file coupling.

Caveats:

- This is a proxy for complexity. It does not measure cyclomatic complexity, test coverage or churn.
- Edge counts come from AST extraction. The `.sql` migrations are not included.
- Some edges are INFERRED and unverified, for example 15 on `createApp()`.

## Priority hotspots

| # | File | LOC | Symbols | Edges | Cross-file links |
|---|------|-----|---------|-------|------------------|
| 1 | `apps/user-ui/src/App.tsx` | 3070 | 94 | 464 | 66 |
| 2 | `apps/agent-runner/src/turn-executor.ts` | 940 | 31 | 210 | 102 |
| 3 | `apps/api/src/app.ts` | 544 | 20 | 166 | 112 |
| 4 | `apps/admin-ui/src/screens/AgentsScreen.tsx` | 1793 | 11 | 59 | 29 |
| 5 | `apps/admin-ui/src/screens/ChatScreen.tsx` | 1456 | 41 | 187 | 31 |
| 6 | `apps/admin-ui/src/App.tsx` | 1385 | 13 | 109 | 71 |
| 7 | `apps/api/src/routes/events.ts` | 1302 | 13 | 81 | 49 |
| 8 | `apps/agent-runner/src/tools/events.ts` | 1195 | 35 | 113 | 11 |
| 9 | `apps/api/src/routes/agents.ts` | 1159 | 23 | 80 | 26 |
| 10 | `apps/api/src/routes/collab.ts` | 1135 | 18 | 77 | 27 |
| 11 | `apps/agent-runner/src/rlm.ts` | 1018 | 38 | 157 | 33 |
| 12 | `apps/opscli/src/index.ts` | 919 | 10 | 111 | 79 |
| 13 | `apps/agent-runner/src/wrapper-harness/command.ts` | 860 | 29 | 127 | 35 |

## Tasks

### 1. Split `apps/user-ui/src/App.tsx`

- [ ] It is the largest file, with the most edges in the graph. It holds the whole user shell: routing, state, data loading and channel/conversation logic.
- [ ] Low runtime risk compared with the runner, so it is a good place to start.
- [ ] Extract routing, data loading and conversation logic into separate modules or hooks.

### 2. Review `apps/agent-runner/src/turn-executor.ts`

- [ ] It is the densest file for its size (210 edges, 102 cross-file links).
- [ ] It contains the mid-turn event injection, which `AGENTS.md` calls the subtlest behavior in the codebase (`reconcileLateInjectedMessages`, `selectRecentDeltaEventsForPrompt`).
- [ ] Measure real cyclomatic complexity before changing it.
- [ ] Check test coverage first. `runner.test.ts` is the de facto behavioral spec.

### 3. Verify and slim `apps/api/src/app.ts`

- [ ] It has the highest cross-file coupling. Some of that is by design, since it is the composition root.
- [ ] `insertEvent()` lives here and is the single write path for every event.
- [ ] Verify the 15 INFERRED edges on `createApp()` (for example with `eventRowToApi()` and `getDefaultSoulPath()`).
- [ ] Keep the rule that route modules receive dependencies through the deps object.

### 4. Break up large admin-UI components

- [ ] `AgentsScreen.tsx` has 1,793 lines but only 11 symbols, which points to a few very large components.
- [ ] `ChatScreen.tsx` has 187 edges.
- [ ] `admin-ui/src/App.tsx` has 71 cross-file links.

### 5. Split large API route modules

- [ ] `routes/events.ts`, `routes/agents.ts` and `routes/collab.ts` are each over 1,100 lines.

### 6. Runner internals

- [ ] `rlm.ts` has 157 edges.
- [ ] `tools/events.ts` has 1,195 lines.
- [ ] `wrapper-harness/command.ts` runs arbitrary host code, which raises the cost of getting it wrong.

## Other findings

- **Big files with few symbols.** `AgentsScreen.tsx`, `admin-ui/App.tsx` and `opscli/src/index.ts` (919 lines, 10 symbols) suggest very large functions or components.
- **High fan-in type modules.** `apps/admin-ui/src/types.ts` has 103 cross-file links. `agent-runner/src/types.ts` is only 37 lines but has 81. Changes to either ripple widely.
- **Duplicated UI plumbing.** `admin-ui` and `user-ui` each have their own `App()`, `apiFetch`, `getApiHeaders` and `config.ts`. A fix in one may need repeating in the other.
- **Weak community cohesion.** The report flags "UI Button Primitives" (0.12) and "Wrapper Harness Runtime" (0.08) as weakly interconnected.

## Notes

- Follow the repo's TDD and testing conventions: add or confirm behavioral tests before each refactor. Commit before refactoring, and commit refactors separately from feature work.
- Re-run `/graphify . --update` after refactors to see whether coupling drops.

content.text:
I read all of `apps/user-ui/src/App.tsx` (3,070 lines), plus `api.ts`, `config.ts` and `types.ts`. The path is `apps/user-ui`, not `users-ui`. This is the plan. I haven't changed any code.

## 1. Characterisation tests

**Starting point:** user-ui has no test tooling at all: no jsdom, Testing Library or MSW. Root `vitest` only runs node tests.

**Approach:** mount the real `<App />` and drive it like a user. Fake only the outside world:
- **HTTP:** MSW, or a stubbed `fetch`, answering `/api/*`. I'd assert on the requests the app makes (method, URL, body), since that is its real contract.
- **WebSocket:** a fake `WebSocket` class that the test can push events through.
- **Browser:** `history`/`location`, `clipboard`, `window.confirm`, `requestAnimationFrame` and fake timers.

Tests never import `api.ts`, `config.ts` or any internal module, and never mock them. Otherwise moving those modules would force test edits. They import only `App`, the types from `types.ts`, and factory functions (`getMockChannel`, `getMockEvent`, …). No `let` or `beforeEach`.

**Setup:** add `jsdom`, `@testing-library/react`, `user-event`, `jest-dom` and `msw`. Use a per-file `@vitest-environment jsdom` so the node suites are untouched.

**Behaviours to pin, by area:**
- **Auth:**
  - Session check on load, then the login form and its error.
  - The forced password change: it needs at least 8 characters and a matching confirmation, and the submit button stays disabled until both hold.
  - Sign-out resets the UI.
- **Workspace load:**
  - `?share=` token claim, including the failure path.
  - `?channel=` deep link.
  - Falling back to the first non-archived visible channel.
  - Archived channels auto-expanding.
- **Sidebar:**
  - Visibility rules for private, public, team-shared, DM and lifecycle channels.
  - Grouping into Direct, Channels and Shared.
  - Search, which force-expands groups.
  - Unread badges.
  - Display names such as "you" and `Direct: a, b`.
- **Timeline:**
  - Message vs trace grouping.
  - Hidden `ui.json-render.action` messages.
  - Markdown, json-render and secret-input rendering.
  - The failure-classification rules (the first matching rule wins).
  - Trace chips and detail expansion.
  - Attachments.
  - Sensitive-message reveal and hide.
  - "Agent is thinking", and the offline-agent hint.
- **Loading:**
  - Initial load and "Load previous messages".
  - Realtime merge and dedupe.
  - "New messages below", with `scrollHeight` stubbed.
  - Polling every 10s only while the WebSocket is down.
  - WebSocket reconnect backoff.
  - Topic subscribe and unsubscribe as visible channels change.
- **Composer:**
  - Enter vs Shift+Enter.
  - Disabled states for archived, read-only and sending.
  - Attachment upload, ready and error states, plus paste-image upload.
  - The "Attached N files" fallback text.
- **Dialogs and management:**
  - Cmd+K opens the conversation dialog and Esc closes it.
  - DM-vs-channel creation rules.
  - Manage channel: save diff, archive, delete with confirm.
  - Add and remove participants and shares.
  - Copy share link.

**Gaps and risks:**
- These tests pass the moment they're written. To check they would catch a break, I'd run coverage on `App.tsx` as a gap-finder and manually break the code in a few places. This is a deliberate exception to RED-first, since there is nothing to turn red.
- jsdom has no layout, so scroll and autosize behaviour is only partly testable. I'd stub the layout properties and accept partial coverage there.
- I'd pin quirks as they are and log them separately, without fixing them mid-refactor. One I already spotted: `DIRECT_GROUP` and `AGENT_AGENT_DM` channels pass the visibility rule but match no sidebar group, so they never get listed.

## 2. Analysis and target architecture

`App.tsx` mixes five concerns in a single function:
- **Pure domain rules (lines 20–594, plus inline `useMemo`s):** event interpretation, trace and failure classification, channel visibility and grouping, event ordering, attachment parsing, timeline grouping.
- **Use cases (about 17 handlers):** sign in/out, change password, load workspace, load/older messages, send, upload, start conversation, delete/save channel, participants, shares, share link, reveal sensitive.
- **Infrastructure:**
  - `fetch`, `WebSocket` with reconnect, and polling.
  - `history`/`URL`, `clipboard`, `confirm`, `rAF` and `navigator.connection`.
- **State:** about 60 `useState`s and 16 refs. Many refs only mirror state so that WebSocket callbacks avoid stale closures. The unread/last-seen logic is spread across four places.
- **Presentation:** about 900 lines of JSX covering 2 auth screens, a sidebar, a timeline, a composer, a side panel and 3 dialogs. The markdown/json-render/secret-input block is duplicated verbatim for sensitive content.

**Proposed shape (pragmatic hexagonal, no classes, factories as in the repo):**
```
src/
  domain/{identity,conversations,messaging}/   pure TS, no React
  application/                                 use cases: (options) => result, ports injected
  ports/                                       interfaces: Backend gateways, RealtimeFeed, DeepLink, Clipboard, Confirm
  infrastructure/                              http, websocket, browser adapters (today's api.ts/config.ts move here)
  ui/{auth,sidebar,timeline,composer,dialogs}/ components + hooks (driving adapter)
  App.tsx                                      composition root only
```
- **Bounded contexts:**
  - **Identity** (session, password).
  - **Conversations** (channels, visibility, grouping, participants, shares, archive, deep link, plus an agent/human directory read model).
  - **Messaging** (event stream, timeline, trace, attachments, sensitive content, unread, pagination).
- **State:** the three auth booleans become one `signedOut | loading | mustChangePassword | ready` union. Each context gets a reducer, which removes the ref mirrors.
- **Dependency rule:** `domain` imports nothing, `application` imports `domain` and `ports`, and `ui` imports `application`. A small guard test enforces this.
- **Trade-off:** I wouldn't create a port for every browser API. I'd keep ports where they give a test seam or hide a real boundary, and leave scrolling and autosize as plain UI hooks.

## 3. Step plan

Every step ends with the characterisation tests unchanged and green, `npm run lint` and `npm test` green, `npm run build` for user-ui green, a quick manual smoke with `ORGOPS_LLM_STUB=1`, and a commit.

0. **Safety net:** tooling plus the test suites above, committed one area at a time. Nothing in `App.tsx` changes.
1. **Move pure functions out** into `domain/*`, verbatim, in several small commits: event interpretation, trace and failure rules, channel rules, ordering and attachments.
2. **Extract presentational components,** props in and callbacks out, one per commit: auth screens, dialogs, sidebar, activity panel, composer, timeline items. De-duplicate the markdown block here.
3. **Introduce gateway ports and HTTP adapters:** `ConversationGateway`, `MessageGateway`, `FileGateway`, `SessionGateway`, plus `DeepLink`, `Clipboard` and `Confirm`. Swap call sites one at a time.
4. **Extract realtime:** a `RealtimeFeed` adapter (connect, backoff, topic diff) and a polling-fallback hook.
5. **Identity context:** use cases, the session state union and `useSession`.
6. **Conversations context:** reducer and use cases (load workspace, select, start, manage, participants, shares, share link).
7. **Messaging context:** timeline load and pagination, a single unread tracker, send, upload, sensitive reveal, and the scroll hook.
8. **`App.tsx` becomes the composition root** (about 100 lines or fewer), wiring adapters through context.
9. **Hardening:**
   - The dependency-direction guard test.
   - Update the user-ui section of `docs/SPEC.md` and the architecture notes in `AGENTS.md`.
   - Re-run `/graphify . --update` to measure the coupling drop.
   - Triage the logged quirks into separate fix tickets, each with its own test.

**Pitfalls to watch:**
- Effect ordering. The reset effect on `activeChannelId` must run before the load effect.
- Closures that read render-time values (`loadShell`, `loadMessageNotifications`). The tests must pin the current behaviour before the closures are replaced.

**Decisions where I'd go with these defaults unless you object:**
- **Test stack:** jsdom + MSW + Testing Library rather than Playwright. A small Playwright smoke test could come later.
- **Existing `as` assertions:** carry them over verbatim when moving code. Replace them with schema parsing at the gateways in a separate commit, which would add a `zod` dependency to user-ui.
- **Folder layout:** inside `apps/user-ui/src`, not new packages.

Want me to save this as `docs/user-ui-refactoring-plan.md` and start on step 0?

message.content: For the tests - we should make sure they run fast. And if they do, probably experiment with mutation testing to make sure they cover the right behavior

content.text:
Both fit the plan. Here is how I'd build them in.

## Keeping the tests fast

I'd set a budget before writing any tests: the whole characterisation suite under about 10 seconds, and any single test under about 200ms. The choices below serve that.

- **Environment:** use `happy-dom` instead of `jsdom`. It starts faster and renders faster. If a behaviour only works in jsdom, I'd switch that one file back.
- **Network:** a hand-rolled `fetch` stub with a route table, instead of MSW. MSW is more realistic but adds interception overhead per request. The app only uses `fetch` and `WebSocket`, so a stub is enough, and the tests still assert on method, URL and body. I'd keep one or two MSW-backed tests only if the stub proves too lenient.
- **Time:** fake timers everywhere, so the 10s polling, the 2s "Link copied" reset and the reconnect backoff cost nothing. No real `waitFor` timeouts. I'd advance the fake clock and flush promises instead.
- **Input:** `fireEvent` for plain state changes, and `user-event` only where realistic typing matters (Enter vs Shift+Enter, IME composition). `user-event` is the slowest part of most suites.
- **Isolation:** vitest runs files in parallel workers, so I'd split the suites by area (auth, sidebar, timeline, realtime, composer, dialogs). Each test renders a fresh `App` with its own factory data, which keeps tests independent and cheap.
- **Fixtures:** small factory data. A channel list of 3 is enough, with no big realistic payloads.
- **Measurement:** a timing check in the first PR (`vitest --reporter=verbose`). If one test goes over budget, I'd fix it then, not later.

## Mutation testing

I'd use **Stryker** with its vitest runner. A mutation run is only practical if the tests are fast, so the speed work comes first, as you said.

- **Scope:** mutate only `apps/user-ui/src/**` (excluding `*.test.*` and `styles.css`). Run it per step, not in CI at first.
- **Speed settings:**
  - Per-test coverage analysis, so each mutant runs only the tests that touch it.
  - Incremental mode, so later runs only retest changed code.
  - Mutate the extracted modules from step 1 separately. `App.tsx` at 3,070 lines would generate thousands of mutants in the first run.
- **Reading the output:**
  - Surviving mutants in conditionals, string literals and arithmetic mean untested behaviour. I'd add a test per real gap.
  - I'd ignore survivors in class names, `aria-*` strings and style code. Those are equivalent mutants or implementation detail, and chasing them would couple tests to markup.
  - Target a mutation score of roughly 80% on the logic modules, not 100%.
- **Order:** run it once the first suites are green and fast, to find gaps in the safety net. Then run it again after each extraction step as a regression check on the tests themselves. This replaces my earlier "manually break the code in a few places" idea.

**Caveat:** Stryker's vitest runner needs to match vitest 5 (the repo's current version). I haven't verified that, so the first thing I'd do is a small spike: install it, run it against one extracted file, and confirm the runner works and the time per run is acceptable. If it doesn't work, the fallback is a hand-picked list of manual mutations.

**Plan change:** step 0 splits into 0a (tooling plus timing budget), 0b (suites, one area per commit) and 0c (the Stryker spike, then the gap-filling pass). Refactoring doesn't start until 0c is done.

I'd go with `happy-dom` and the hand-rolled `fetch` stub by default. Should I save the plan with these changes and start step 0a?

# Refactoring plan: `apps/user-ui/src/App.tsx`

`App.tsx` is 3,070 lines: the largest file and the most coupled one in the repo (see `docs/refactoring-todo.md`, task 1). This plan covers three parts:

1. Characterisation tests that pin the current behaviour.
2. Analysis and target architecture (hexagonal, DDD).
3. A step plan in which every step leaves a working app.

Starting point: `apps/user-ui` has no test tooling (no DOM environment, no Testing Library). Root `vitest` only runs node tests.

## 1. Characterisation tests

### Approach

Mount the real `<App />` and drive it like a user. Fake only the outside world:

- **HTTP:** a hand-rolled `fetch` stub with a route table. Assert on the requests the app makes (method, URL, body), since that is its real contract.
- **WebSocket:** a fake `WebSocket` class that the test can push events through.
- **Browser:** `history`/`location`, `clipboard`, `window.confirm`, `requestAnimationFrame`, fake timers.

Tests never import `api.ts`, `config.ts` or any internal module, and never mock them. Otherwise moving those modules would force test edits. They import only `App`, the types from `types.ts`, and factory functions (`getMockChannel`, `getMockEvent`, ...). No `let` or `beforeEach`.

### Behaviours to pin

- **Auth:**
  - Session check on load, then the login form and its error.
  - Forced password change: at least 8 characters and a matching confirmation, and the submit button stays disabled until both hold.
  - Sign-out resets the UI.
- **Workspace load:**
  - `?share=` token claim, including the failure path.
  - `?channel=` deep link.
  - Fallback to the first non-archived visible channel.
  - Archived channels auto-expanding.
- **Sidebar:**
  - Visibility rules for private, public, team-shared, DM and lifecycle channels.
  - Grouping into Direct, Channels and Shared.
  - Search, which force-expands groups.
  - Unread badges.
  - Display names such as "you" and `Direct: a, b`.
- **Timeline:**
  - Message vs trace grouping.
  - Hidden `ui.json-render.action` messages.
  - Markdown, json-render and secret-input rendering.
  - Failure classification (first matching rule wins).
  - Trace chips and detail expansion.
  - Attachments.
  - Sensitive-message reveal and hide.
  - "Agent is thinking" and the offline-agent hint.
- **Loading:**
  - Initial load and "Load previous messages".
  - Realtime merge and dedupe.
  - "New messages below", with `scrollHeight` stubbed.
  - Polling every 10s only while the WebSocket is down.
  - WebSocket reconnect backoff.
  - Topic subscribe and unsubscribe as visible channels change.
- **Composer:**
  - Enter vs Shift+Enter.
  - Disabled states for archived, read-only and sending.
  - Attachment upload (ready and error states) and paste-image upload.
  - The "Attached N files" fallback text.
- **Dialogs and management:**
  - Cmd+K opens the conversation dialog and Esc closes it.
  - DM-vs-channel creation rules.
  - Manage channel: save diff, archive, delete with confirm.
  - Add and remove participants and shares.
  - Copy share link.

### Speed budget

The whole characterisation suite should run in under about 10 seconds, and any single test in under about 200ms.

- **Environment:** `happy-dom` rather than `jsdom`. Switch an individual file back to `jsdom` only if a behaviour needs it.
- **Network:** the hand-rolled `fetch` stub, not MSW, to avoid per-request interception overhead. Keep one or two MSW-backed tests only if the stub proves too lenient.
- **Time:** fake timers everywhere, so the 10s polling, the 2s "Link copied" reset and the reconnect backoff cost nothing. No real `waitFor` timeouts; advance the fake clock and flush promises.
- **Input:** `fireEvent` for plain state changes. `user-event` only where realistic typing matters (Enter vs Shift+Enter, IME composition).
- **Isolation:** suites split by area (auth, sidebar, timeline, realtime, composer, dialogs) so vitest runs them in parallel. Each test renders a fresh `App` with its own factory data.
- **Fixtures:** small factory data (for example 3 channels).
- **Measurement:** check timings in the first PR (`vitest --reporter=verbose`) and fix anything over budget immediately.

### Mutation testing

Use **Stryker** with its vitest runner to check that the tests cover the right behaviour.

- **Scope:** mutate only `apps/user-ui/src/**`, excluding `*.test.*` and `styles.css`. Run it per step, not in CI at first.
- **Speed settings:** per-test coverage analysis and incremental mode. Mutate the extracted modules from step 1 separately, because `App.tsx` as a whole would generate thousands of mutants on the first run.
- **Reading the output:**
  - Survivors in conditionals, string literals and arithmetic indicate untested behaviour. Add a test for each real gap.
  - Ignore survivors in class names, `aria-*` strings and style code. They are equivalent mutants or implementation detail, and chasing them would couple the tests to markup.
  - Target roughly 80% on logic modules, not 100%.
- **When to run it:** once after the first suites are green and fast, to find gaps. Then after each extraction step as a regression check on the tests themselves.
- **Caveat:** the Stryker vitest runner must support the repo's vitest version (5.x). This is unverified, so step 0c starts with a spike. Fallback if it does not work: a hand-picked list of manual mutations.

### Gaps and risks

- Characterisation tests pass the moment they are written. Mutation testing replaces RED-first as the check that they would catch a break. This is a deliberate exception to the usual TDD rule, since there is nothing to turn red.
- Happy-dom and jsdom have no layout, so scroll and autosize behaviour is only partly testable. Stub the layout properties and accept partial coverage there.
- Pin quirks as they are and log them separately. Do not fix them mid-refactor. One already spotted: `DIRECT_GROUP` and `AGENT_AGENT_DM` channels pass the visibility rule but match no sidebar group, so they are never listed.

## 2. Analysis and target architecture

`App.tsx` mixes five concerns in a single function:

- **Pure domain rules** (lines 20-594, plus inline `useMemo`s): event interpretation, trace and failure classification, channel visibility and grouping, event ordering, attachment parsing, timeline grouping.
- **Use cases** (about 17 handlers): sign in/out, change password, load workspace, load/older messages, send, upload, start conversation, delete/save channel, participants, shares, share link, reveal sensitive.
- **Infrastructure:** `fetch`, `WebSocket` with reconnect, polling, `history`/`URL`, `clipboard`, `confirm`, `rAF`, `navigator.connection`.
- **State:** about 60 `useState`s and 16 refs. Many refs only mirror state so that WebSocket callbacks avoid stale closures. The unread/last-seen logic is spread across four places.
- **Presentation:** about 900 lines of JSX covering 2 auth screens, a sidebar, a timeline, a composer, a side panel and 3 dialogs. The markdown/json-render/secret-input block is duplicated verbatim for sensitive content.

### Proposed shape

Pragmatic hexagonal: no classes, factory functions as in the rest of the repo.

```
src/
  domain/{identity,conversations,messaging}/   pure TS, no React
  application/                                 use cases: (options) => result, ports injected
  ports/                                       interfaces: gateways, RealtimeFeed, DeepLink, Clipboard, Confirm
  infrastructure/                              http, websocket, browser adapters (api.ts / config.ts move here)
  ui/{auth,sidebar,timeline,composer,dialogs}/ components + hooks (driving adapter)
  App.tsx                                      composition root only
```

- **Bounded contexts:**
  - **Identity:** session, password.
  - **Conversations:** channels, visibility, grouping, participants, shares, archive, deep link, plus an agent/human directory read model.
  - **Messaging:** event stream, timeline, trace, attachments, sensitive content, unread, pagination.
- **State:** the three auth booleans become one `signedOut | loading | mustChangePassword | ready` union. Each context gets a reducer, which removes the ref mirrors.
- **Dependency rule:** `domain` imports nothing, `application` imports `domain` and `ports`, `ui` imports `application`. A guard test enforces it.
- **Trade-off:** no port for every browser API. Keep ports where they give a test seam or hide a real boundary. Scrolling and autosize stay plain UI hooks.

## 3. Step plan

Every step ends with the characterisation tests unchanged and green, `npm run lint` and `npm test` green, the user-ui build green, a quick manual smoke with `ORGOPS_LLM_STUB=1`, and a commit.

**0. Safety net** (no changes to `App.tsx`)

- **0a:** tooling (`happy-dom`, Testing Library, test setup) and the timing budget.
- **0b:** the suites above, one area per commit.
- **0c:** Stryker spike, then a gap-filling pass driven by surviving mutants. Refactoring does not start until this is done.

**1. Move pure functions out** into `domain/*`, verbatim, in several small commits: event interpretation, trace and failure rules, channel rules, ordering and attachments.

**2. Extract presentational components,** props in and callbacks out, one per commit: auth screens, dialogs, sidebar, activity panel, composer, timeline items. De-duplicate the markdown block here.

**3. Introduce gateway ports and HTTP adapters:** `ConversationGateway`, `MessageGateway`, `FileGateway`, `SessionGateway`, plus `DeepLink`, `Clipboard` and `Confirm`. Swap call sites one at a time.

**4. Extract realtime:** a `RealtimeFeed` adapter (connect, backoff, topic diff) and a polling-fallback hook.

**5. Identity context:** use cases, the session state union and `useSession`.

**6. Conversations context:** reducer and use cases (load workspace, select, start, manage, participants, shares, share link).

**7. Messaging context:** timeline load and pagination, a single unread tracker, send, upload, sensitive reveal, and the scroll hook.

**8. `App.tsx` becomes the composition root** (about 100 lines or fewer), wiring adapters through context.

**9. Hardening:**

- The dependency-direction guard test.
- Update the user-ui section of `docs/SPEC.md` and the architecture notes in `AGENTS.md`.
- Re-run `/graphify . --update` to measure the coupling drop.
- Triage the logged quirks into separate fix tickets, each with its own test.

### Pitfalls

- **Effect ordering:** the reset effect on `activeChannelId` must run before the load effect.
- **Render-time closures:** `loadShell` and `loadMessageNotifications` read values from the render closure. Pin the current behaviour before replacing the closures.
- **Existing `as` assertions:** carry them over verbatim when moving code. Replace them with schema parsing at the gateways in a separate commit (this adds a `zod` dependency to user-ui).

### Defaults chosen (override if needed)

- **Test stack:** `happy-dom` plus a hand-rolled `fetch` stub rather than Playwright or MSW. A small Playwright smoke test could come later.
- **Folder layout:** inside `apps/user-ui/src`, not new packages.
- **Schema parsing:** deferred to its own commit after step 3.

- **Speed settings:** per-test coverage analysis and incremental mode. Mutate the extracted modules from step 1 separately, because `App.tsx` as a whole would generate thousands of mutants on the first run.
- **Reading the output:**
  - Survivors in conditionals, string literals and arithmetic indicate untested behaviour. Add a test for each real gap.
  - Ignore survivors in class names, `aria-*` strings and style code. They are equivalent mutants or implementation detail, and chasing them would couple the tests to markup.
  - Target roughly 80% on logic modules, not 100%.
- **When to run it:** once after the first suites are green and fast, to find gaps. Then after each extraction step as a regression check on the tests themselves.
- **Caveat:** the Stryker vitest runner must support the repo's vitest version (5.x). This is unverified, so step 0c starts with a spike. Fallback if it does not work: a hand-picked list of manual mutations.

### Gaps and risks

- Characterisation tests pass the moment they are written. Mutation testing replaces RED-first as the check that they would catch a break. This is a deliberate exception to the usual TDD rule, since there is nothing to turn red.
- Happy-dom and jsdom have no layout, so scroll and autosize behaviour is only partly testable. Stub the layout properties and accept partial coverage there.
- Pin quirks as they are and log them separately. Do not fix them mid-refactor. One already spotted: `DIRECT_GROUP` and `AGENT_AGENT_DM` channels pass the visibility rule but match no sidebar group, so they are never listed.

## 2. Analysis and target architecture

`App.tsx` mixes five concerns in a single function:

- **Pure domain rules** (lines 20-594, plus inline `useMemo`s): event interpretation, trace and failure classification, channel visibility and grouping, event ordering, attachment parsing, timeline grouping.
- **Use cases** (about 17 handlers): sign in/out, change password, load workspace, load/older messages, send, upload, start conversation, delete/save channel, participants, shares, share link, reveal sensitive.
- **Infrastructure:** `fetch`, `WebSocket` with reconnect, polling, `history`/`URL`, `clipboard`, `confirm`, `rAF`, `navigator.connection`.
- **State:** about 60 `useState`s and 16 refs. Many refs only mirror state so that WebSocket callbacks avoid stale closures. The unread/last-seen logic is spread across four places.
- **Presentation:** about 900 lines of JSX covering 2 auth screens, a sidebar, a timeline, a composer, a side panel and 3 dialogs. The markdown/json-render/secret-input block is duplicated verbatim for sensitive content.

### Proposed shape

Pragmatic hexagonal: no classes, factory functions as in the rest of the repo.

```
src/
  domain/{identity,conversations,messaging}/   pure TS, no React
  application/                                 use cases: (options) => result, ports injected
  ports/                                       interfaces: gateways, RealtimeFeed, DeepLink, Clipboard, Confirm
  infrastructure/                              http, websocket, browser adapters (api.ts / config.ts move here)
  ui/{auth,sidebar,timeline,composer,dialogs}/ components + hooks (driving adapter)
  App.tsx                                      composition root only
```

- **Bounded contexts:**
  - **Identity:** session, password.
  - **Conversations:** channels, visibility, grouping, participants, shares, archive, deep link, plus an agent/human directory read model.
  - **Messaging:** event stream, timeline, trace, attachments, sensitive content, unread, pagination.
- **State:** the three auth booleans become one `signedOut | loading | mustChangePassword | ready` union. Each context gets a reducer, which removes the ref mirrors.
- **Dependency rule:** `domain` imports nothing, `application` imports `domain` and `ports`, `ui` imports `application`. A guard test enforces it.
- **Trade-off:** no port for every browser API. Keep ports where they give a test seam or hide a real boundary. Scrolling and autosize stay plain UI hooks.

## 3. Step plan

Every step ends with the characterisation tests unchanged and green, `npm run lint` and `npm test` green, the user-ui build green, a quick manual smoke with `ORGOPS_LLM_STUB=1`, and a commit.

**0. Safety net** (no changes to `App.tsx`)

- **0a:** tooling (`happy-dom`, Testing Library, test setup) and the timing budget.
- **0b:** the suites above, one area per commit.
- **0c:** Stryker spike, then a gap-filling pass driven by surviving mutants. Refactoring does not start until this is done.

**1. Move pure functions out** into `domain/*`, verbatim, in several small commits: event interpretation, trace and failure rules, channel rules, ordering and attachments.

**2. Extract presentational components,** props in and callbacks out, one per commit: auth screens, dialogs, sidebar, activity panel, composer, timeline items. De-duplicate the markdown block here.

**3. Introduce gateway ports and HTTP adapters:** `ConversationGateway`, `MessageGateway`, `FileGateway`, `SessionGateway`, plus `DeepLink`, `Clipboard` and `Confirm`. Swap call sites one at a time.

**4. Extract realtime:** a `RealtimeFeed` adapter (connect, backoff, topic diff) and a polling-fallback hook.

**5. Identity context:** use cases, the session state union and `useSession`.

**6. Conversations context:** reducer and use cases (load workspace, select, start, manage, participants, shares, share link).

**7. Messaging context:** timeline load and pagination, a single unread tracker, send, upload, sensitive reveal, and the scroll hook.

**8. `App.tsx` becomes the composition root** (about 100 lines or fewer), wiring adapters through context.

**9. Hardening:**

- The dependency-direction guard test.
- Update the user-ui section of `docs/SPEC.md` and the architecture notes in `AGENTS.md`.
- Re-run `/graphify . --update` to measure the coupling drop.
- Triage the logged quirks into separate fix tickets, each with its own test.

### Pitfalls

- **Effect ordering:** the reset effect on `activeChannelId` must run before the load effect.
- **Render-time closures:** `loadShell` and `loadMessageNotifications` read values from the render closure. Pin the current behaviour before replacing the closures.
- **Existing `as` assertions:** carry them over verbatim when moving code. Replace them with schema parsing at the gateways in a separate commit (this adds a `zod` dependency to user-ui).

### Defaults chosen (override if needed)

- **Test stack:** `happy-dom` plus a hand-rolled `fetch` stub rather than Playwright or MSW. A small Playwright smoke test could come later.
- **Folder layout:** inside `apps/user-ui/src`, not new packages.
- **Schema parsing:** deferred to its own commit after step 3.
